## Summary (human-written)
<!-- Write this yourself, not with an AI tool. 2-5 sentences: the problem, why
     this approach, and what you checked yourself. -->

## Why

Shared global KV and index state can outlive the stage that produced them. A conventional single-hidden-state pipeline would drop those tensors or their backward routes. Mutable model caches would also mix state from outstanding microbatches under an interleaved schedule.

**Example.**

```text
stage A: producer -> (residual, next_mix, global_KV, index_KV, IDs, scores, candidates)
                              | explicit payload, owned by this microbatch
stage B: consumers -----------+ -> updated payload -> stage C
backward: residual/global_KV/index-score gradients return to their producers
```

## What changed

- Enable existing TP/EP sharding and real pipeline execution.
- Supply static forward/backward metadata for seven boundary tensors through the shared factory included in `1/n`.
- Preserve shared state as explicit per-forward arguments, including interleaved four-stage execution.
- Validate complete, ordered block splits and exactly-once ownership of enabled input/output modules; require a fixed dataloader document bound, keep CP>1 unsupported, and reject fake PP. DSpark requires TP=1; tensor-parallel backbone configs explicitly disable the drafter.
- Register real TP2/EP2 and combined FSDP2/TP2/PP2/EP2 training in the appropriate CI suites. The combined numerical factory uses reference attention; a separate factory selects fused attention-gym kernels.
- Add pipeline gradient/lifetime tests and current architecture/validation documentation.

## User-facing changes

| Before | After |
| --- | --- |
| Backbone supports FSDP with TP=EP=PP=1 | Existing TP/EP and real PP support the backbone |
| No pipeline shared-state contract | Seven explicit tensors with static forward/backward metadata |
| No distributed V4.1 CI selection | Fused two-GPU TP/EP plus combined eight-GPU numerical recipes |

CI catalogue entries and model-index links are mechanical. Boundary state, gradient routes, and split validation require correctness review.

## Numerics / performance

All local comparisons start from one checkpoint and eight distinct packed microbatches: 216 valid global CE labels, 224 routing tokens, actual engine/optimizer hooks, seed 42 and strict determinism. Gradients are reconstructed before clipping, counting all 285 logical parameters once.

| Topology | Compute | Loss error | Gradient max error | Gradient norm ratio | Router counts/biases |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| FSDP2 | BF16 | 0 | `2.79e-9` | `1.00000000018` | Exact |
| FSDP2 + EP2 | BF16 | 0 | `4.66e-7` | `1.00000000367` | Exact |
| PP2, four virtual stages | BF16 | 0 | `1.53e-6` | `0.99999999155` | Exact |
| TP2 + EP2 | BF16 | `5.25e-5` | `2.54e-4` | `0.99997558` | 18 count differences; max bias error `8.75e-4` |
| PP2, four virtual stages | FP32 | 0 | `5.82e-11` | `1.00000000000` | Exact |
| TP2 + EP2 | FP32 | `4.77e-7` | `4.72e-6` | `1.00000000034` | Exact |
| FSDP2 + TP2 + PP2 + EP2, GB200 | BF16 | `5.29e-5` | `2.54e-4` | `0.99997561` | 18 count differences; max bias error `8.75e-4` |
| FSDP2 + TP2 + PP2 + EP2, GB200 | FP32 | 0 | `4.72e-6` | `1.00000000690` | Exact |

BF16 TP changes eleven valid tokens' expert choices at near-tied score boundaries. Holding expert IDs fixed restores counters/biases but leaves BF16 partial-reduction/quantization rounding. FP32 TP/EP passes PyTorch's default FP32 tolerance for every gradient, cosine `0.999999999678`. Different topologies do not promise bitwise AdamW updates: tiny near-zero gradient sign differences can be amplified by its epsilon.

The real eight-GB200 combined gradient comparison passed PyTorch's default FP32 tolerance for all 285 reconstructed gradients, with loss error zero and gradient cosine `0.999999999609`. All eight parent ranks and 18 BF16/FP32 matrix children are bound to the scheduler app ID and verified source/runtime.

Two independent native `loss_compare.py` launches each completed ten C4 optimizer steps on eight GB200 GPUs, with bitwise-identical full-precision loss and grad_norm at every step. Loss changed from `7.664351940155029` to `6.559906482696533`. Both launches verify the same frozen source, complete published runtime, and identical CPU seed payloads. A distinct native import replay with `--assert-equal` completed ten steps on eight GB300 GPUs in the author-selected DCT pool; all ten loss/norm pairs and the seed payload exactly match the eight-GB200 golden. This cross-hardware result covers the reference-attention debug recipe with the same published runtime. The fresh golden SHA256 is `3f21fa384049a96ab70ab855b90e59c4941da6f9ebd6796770ffe3ea9e150213`. `tests/assets/deepseek_v4_1/numerical_golden.json` records the pinned source/runtime, native commands, job IDs, and proof hashes.

The current stack is based on upstream `a87db08ea73cbdd567ceb055bd9118fd4a4507b2`. Four files use the current direct `ParallelismConfig` import and explicit TensorBoard logger API; all 14 model Python files remain byte-identical to the original golden source. A separate native replay of current source `14ba8df0bf471b97c14fe5c3a76c87db7a5ada4a` completed ten steps on eight GB300s in DCT. All ten full-precision loss/norm pairs and the CPU seed payload match the original golden bitwise. Its eight parents and nine native children verified all 1,134 source files and the unchanged published runtime. The source comparison explicitly verifies the four API migrations. `current_main_import_replay` in the provenance asset records this replay separately from the original exports.

| Native validation | Source | GPUs | Result |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| [Independent export A](https://www.internalfb.com/msl/studio/runs/mast/dsv41-stack-a-final-20261103-v6-pg0k6vr0) | `da6b26f9` | 8 GB200 | Ten optimizer steps completed |
| [Independent export B](https://www.internalfb.com/msl/studio/runs/mast/dsv41-stack-b-final-20261103-v6-fj1qh9wv) | `da6b26f9` | 8 GB200 | All ten loss/norm pairs bitwise equal to A |
| [Original source import](https://www.internalfb.com/msl/studio/runs/mast/dsv41-stack-replay-final-20261103-v8-gb300-lnt2s1bq) | `da6b26f9` | 8 GB300 | `--assert-equal` passes all ten loss/norm pairs against the fresh golden |
| [Current upstream source import](https://www.internalfb.com/msl/studio/runs/mast/dsv41-stack-replay-final-20261103-v10-current-main-hsxssbgf) | `14ba8df0` | 8 GB300 | `--assert-equal` passes all ten original golden loss/norm pairs |

## Testing

69 CPU model/integration-definition tests passed on the current upstream base. Nine pipeline cases cover three splits and no/default/full remat with two outstanding packed forwards, exact logits/loss/every gradient/buffer, and real boundary shape/dtype/stride/gradient metadata. Focused invalid-split cases guard missing/misplaced output, vision, and drafter modules; two config cases reject unsupported drafter TP with and without sequence parallelism. A packed-document regression demonstrates why PP rejects unbounded document metadata. All-file pre-commit passes. The native CPU seed/checkpoint and selected fused TP2/EP2 recipe completed ten training steps with SPMD checking enabled in the complete ARM Python 3.12 environment (published PyTorch `2.16.0.dev20261030+cu132`, `torch_checkpointing 0.1.1`, CUTLASS DSL `4.7.0`); all losses and norms are finite, with loss `7.677572250366211` -> `6.613213539123535`. Each native child verified the source, helpers, dependency versions, and published PyTorch file hashes before computation. The earlier vision/drafter FSDP checks and fresh native V4 FSDP2 regression remain passing.

Full-size convergence, released weight-value loading, H100 execution, CP>1, packed incremental cache allocation, and optimized serving prefill remain outside the validated scope. No throughput improvement is claimed.

## Commit regrouping and validation provenance

This increment retains the complete file tree of the previously validated and pushed commit `ecd5c9c7e86bae579ad3f052f77308e6b7bd7729`. Its preceding model milestone is also unchanged, so the incremental source diff and existing validation are preserved. Original test, runtime, and golden source bindings are retained rather than relabeled.

Stack position: `4/n`; base `stack-dsv41/03-dspark`.
